name: apt
description: The high-level Debian/Ubuntu package tool: installs, upgrades, and removes software with automatic dependency resolution.

flags.description: Refresh the package index from repositories (does not upgrade anything).
Install available upgrades of all installed packages.
Like upgrade but may remove packages to resolve conflicts.
Install a package (add -y to skip confirmation).
Remove a package, keeping its configuration files.
Remove a package AND its configuration files.
Show package details: version, size, dependencies.
List installed packages; --upgradable lists pending updates.
Remove packages that were auto-installed as dependencies and are no longer needed.

examples.command: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y
examples.explanation: The daily routine: refresh the index, then apply all available updates non-interactively.

examples.command: sudo apt install nginx git curl
examples.explanation: Installs several packages, resolving all dependencies automatically.
Searches package names and descriptions in the configured repositories.
Displays version, size, and dependencies before installing.

examples.command: sudo apt remove nginx && sudo apt purge nginx
examples.explanation: remove keeps /etc/nginx; purge deletes it too.
Cleans up orphaned dependencies after removals.

about: apt (since Debian 8/Ubuntu 16.04) is the friendly front end combining the most-used apt-get and apt-cache commands, with a nicer progress output. apt-get remains the stable, scriptable interface with an unchanging output contract; prefer it in scripts. Both work on .deb-based systems: Debian, Ubuntu, Mint, Kali, Raspberry Pi OS.
Under the hood sits dpkg, which installs individual .deb files but does not resolve dependencies — that is apt's job.
useCases: Install and update software on Debian-family systems.
mistakes: Running apt install without apt update first and getting stale versions or missing candidates.
Using apt upgrade expecting distribution upgrades — for release upgrades use do-release-upgrade (Ubuntu).
warnings: Never interrupt apt during a transaction; if it is interrupted, run sudo dpkg --configure -a to recover.
distroNotes: Debian/Ubuntu/Mint/Kali family only. RHEL-family uses dnf/yum, Arch uses pacman, openSUSE uses zypper.
